1 لَغَزَهُ , aor.
لَغُزَ , (TK,) inf. n. لَغْزٌ, (IF, A, Msb, K,) He turned it from its proper mode or manner; distorted it. (IF, A, Msb, K, TA, TK.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] لَغَزَ جِحَرَتَهُ, and ↓ أَلْغَزَهَا , He (a jerboa) made his burrows winding, or tortuous, and perplexing to the enterer thereof. And لَغَزَ فِى حَفْرِهِ, and ↓ أَلْغَزَ , He pursued a winding, or tortuous, course in his burrowing. (A.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
